bonus_mechanics: Own Oklahoma election: for qualified property and qualified improvement property placed in service in a taxable year beginning after 31 Dec 2021, the taxpayer may deduct 100% of cost in the year placed in service, regardless of the federal bonus rate. Federal depreciation on that property (including federal bonus) is added back, so the net is 100% expensing for Oklahoma. Election is irrevocable per property unless the Tax Commission allows otherwise. The 2022 Form 511 had no bonus subtraction or add-back line; the add-back text was added by SB 602 (effective 1 Nov 2023, applies to returns filed on or after 1 Jan 2023).
change_note: HB 3418 enacted 68 O.S. 2358.6A, new for tax year 2022. Emergency rule 710:50-15-69.1 (adopted 27 Sep 2022) requires adding back federal depreciation on elected property in each later year it is claimed.
special_rules: (1) 'Qualified property' means IRC 168(k) qualified property as the Code existed on 1 Jan 2021, for property placed in service after 31 Dec 2021; 'qualified improvement property' means IRC 168(e)(6) as of 1 Jan 2021. (2) Election is irrevocable. (3) Add back federal depreciation on elected property in the year placed in service and in later years (rule 710:50-15-69.1, emergency rule effective through 14 Sep 2023; the permanent rule was not read). (4) Section 179 expensing is expressly allowed to conform to IRC 179. (5) Swine or poultry producers may use 7-year accelerated depreciation (Sch 511-C misc adj 3) and must add back federal depreciation once fully depreciated for Oklahoma (Sch 511-B misc add 2). (6) Pass-through entities make the election and add-back at entity level (710:50-19-5, 710:50-21-1(c)). (7) A 2022 return filed before 1 Oct 2023 without the add-back had to be amended by 30 Jun 2024 per SB 602.

bonus_mechanics: DOR: SB 1507 'disallows bonus depreciation for tax years 2026 and later.' Per secondary summaries (Baker Tilly, a search summary of the bill) the addition equals the difference between the 168(k) deduction applicable to the taxable year and the 168(k) deduction as amended and in effect on 1 Dec 2017, taken in the year property is placed in service, with a corresponding subtraction over the remaining depreciable life (typically 5 or 7 years). Applies to property placed in service in tax years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2026.
change_note: SB 1507, Oregon Laws 2026 ch. 142, effective 5 Jun 2026, disconnects from federal bonus depreciation for 2026 and later. The DOR page notes a referendum petition filed 10 Apr 2026 proposing to repeal the parts of SB 1507 that disconnect from certain federal provisions; signatures were due 4 Jun 2026. Whether it qualified, and so whether SB 1507 is suspended until a vote, was not confirmed: the Oregon Secretary of State initiatives/referendums page read on 2026-10-06 lists no 2026 referendum petition on SB 1507, which is suggestive but not conclusive (the IRR database was not queried).

bonus_mechanics: Federal bonus depreciation is not allowed for PA personal income tax and federal bonus elections do not apply. Depreciation is computed without 168(k): any generally accepted consistent method, MACRS as in effect when the property was placed in service or under the IRC of 1986 whichever is earlier; straight-line (adjusted) where federal and PA basis differ. PA net profits are computed on PA-40 Schedule C, not taken from federal taxable income.
change_note: No 2021 change. Act 53 of 2022 (179 limits) starts with tax years beginning 1 Jan 2023.
special_rules: (1) PA 179 limit for property placed in service 2003-2022 is 25,000 (Bulletin 2023-02); phase-out starts at 200,000 per the DOR TCJA/OBBBA comparison page. (2) The 179 deduction is a business expense usable only against PA net profits (Schedule C class) and cannot reduce net profits below zero; excess carries over indefinitely. (3) 179 property not expensed is depreciated; if the 179 cost differs from federal, use straight-line. (4) Pass-through entity makes the 179 election at entity level; carryover stays with the entity. (5) PA taxes eight income classes and does not net losses across classes. (6) Because 179 offsets only Schedule C net profits, a rental owner (separate rents class) has no PA 179 offset against rent (my reading of the bulletin).

bonus_mechanics: South Carolina does not adopt IRC 168(k): S.C. Code 12-6-50(4) lists 168(k), (l), (m) and (n) 'relating to bonus depreciation' among sections not adopted. 2021 SC1040 instructions, line v (p.18): 'South Carolina does not recognize bonus depreciation in IRC Section 168(k). With or without bonus depreciation, the depreciable life of the property is the same for federal and state purposes. For the tax year the property is placed in service, a taxpayer must add back, on line e of the SC1040, the difference between the depreciation deduction allowed for federal purposes and the deduction that would have been allowed without bonus depreciation. The South Carolina adjusted basis will then be greater than the federal adjusted basis. For all other years of the depreciable life of the property, an additional depreciation deduction is available for South Carolina purposes.' Line e (p.13) repeats the add-back. Net: SC depreciation = regular MACRS with no bonus.
change_note: No 2021 change. The 2021 'New for 2021' page (p.3) states conformity 'through December 31, 2020, unless otherwise provided'. IL 03-17 (24 Jul 2003) records the original 168(k) disallowance.
special_rules: (1) Add-back on SC1040 line e = federal depreciation minus the depreciation allowed without bonus; the extra SC depreciation in later years is a line v subtraction; keep a separate SC depreciation schedule and SC basis for gain or loss (instructions: adjust gain or loss for SC vs federal basis). (2) Same life and MACRS method as federal. (3) Capital Investment Tax Credit property (investments after 30 Jun 1998): reduce SC basis by the credit claimed and add back the resulting reduction in depreciation (line e). (4) Section 199A qualified business income deduction is added back (line e; 12-6-50(19)). (5) Business meals under IRC 274(n) deducted in full federally must be added back: SC allows 50% (line e, 2021 instructions p.13). (6) Out-of-state rental and business income or loss is carved out on lines b and h, so depreciation on out-of-state property is not in SC income. (7) SC NOL: add back federal NOL if larger than the SC NOL; no carryback. (8) The elective 3% flat rate on pass-through active trade or business income (I-335) was not read.
source_citation: 2021 SC1040 Form and Instructions (IITPacket_2021.pdf): 'New for 2021 - Conformity' p.3, 'Things to know before you begin' p.11, line e p.13, line v p.18; S.C. Code 12-6-40(A)(1), 12-6-50(4), (5B), (19) https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t12c006.php
verify_note: Agency instructions read in full on 2026-10-06 (conformity date, line e, line v). bonus_mechanics: Two agency sources. (1) 2025 SC1040 instructions (Aug 2025): line v p.12 repeats the 168(k) non-recognition and the line e add-back of 'the difference between the depreciation deduction allowed for federal purposes and the deduction that would have been allowed without bonus depreciation'; line e p.5 adds 'Add back any federal deductions resulting from IRC sections that South Carolina does not adopt.' (2) Information Letter 26-4 (Revised, 30 Jan 2026) footnote 3: 'OBBBA also made modifications to section 168(k) ... that will take effect for the 2025 tax year. South Carolina specifically does not adopt these provisions. S.C. Code Ann. 12-6-50 ... Therefore, taxpayers claiming these provisions will continue to make these adjustments on their South Carolina return.' So the 100% federal bonus (property acquired after 19 Jan 2025) and the 40% rate for earlier acquisitions are both added back in the placed-in-service year and recovered through additional SC depreciation later.
change_note: SC conforms to the IRC as amended through 31 Dec 2024 (2025 instructions p.1; S.C. Code 12-6-40(A)(1) as currently codified; Act 63 of 2025, S. 507, approved 22 May 2025, per a search result). OBBBA postdates the 2025 session, so SC has not conformed to it. Letter 26-4 lists eight OBBBA items taxpayers must adjust, including 'Business Assets. The amount taxpayers may expense under IRC Section 179 increased to $2.5 million from $1 million.'
special_rules: (1) 179: not following the OBBBA 2.5 million / 4 million. The Letter gives only the pre-OBBBA 1 million base, so the limit and phase-out shown (1,250,000 / 3,130,000) are my derivation: the Code as of 31 Dec 2024 indexes 179(b), and Rev. Proc. 2024-40 (October 2024) set those 2025 amounts; SC itself prints no figure. (2) 168(n): 12-6-50(4) lists 168(n) as not adopted and the new OBBBA 168(n) (qualified production property) is in any case outside the 31 Dec 2024 Code, so the 100% 168(n) allowance is a federal deduction from an unadopted section and is added back under the 2025 line e instruction (my reading). (3) 163(j) is not adopted (12-6-50(5B)) and 199A is added back (12-6-50(19), line e). (4) Capital Investment Tax Credit basis reduction applies as in prior years. (5) The Department said it will issue updated guidance once the Legislature addresses conformity.
source_citation: 2025 SC1040 Instructions (Aug 2025) p.1, line e p.4-5, line v p.12; SC Information Letter #26-4 (Revised) 30 Jan 2026 (https://dor.sc.gov/income-tax-south-carolina-internal-revenue-code-conformity-update), item 8 and footnote 3; S.C. Code 12-6-40(A)(1), 12-6-50(4), (5B), (19)

The 179 limit and phase-out cells are derived (Code as of 31 Dec 2024 plus Rev. Proc. 2024-40) and are not printed by SC; treat as unconfirmed. The 168(n) reading relies on the statute list plus the Code-date argument.

bonus_mechanics: Same as 2025: 168(k) is on the 12-6-50(4) not-adopted list at any IRC date, so federal bonus is added back in the placed-in-service year and recovered through additional SC depreciation over the life. No 2026 form or instruction read (none issued yet).
change_note: No enacted 2026 change found. S.C. Code 12-6-40(A)(1) as codified (fetched 2026-10-06) still reads 'as amended through December 31, 2024'. H. 5167 (conform through 31 Dec 2025, introduced 11 Feb 2026) remained in House Ways and Means. H. 3368 (overtime exclusion bill whose section 1 would move the date to 31 Dec 2025) failed second reading in the Senate on 31 Mar 2026 (16 ayes, 27 nays) per the bill page. S. 507 and H. 3489 were listed but not read for 2026 action.
special_rules: If a later act moves the IRC date to 31 Dec 2025, OBBBA 179 and other items would come in for 2026 while 12-6-50(4) would still exclude 168(k) and 168(n). Until then SC remains at the 31 Dec 2024 date. 179 limit for 2026 under the 31 Dec 2024 Code is unknown (the IRS never published a pre-OBBBA 2026 indexation), so null.
